name: FERAL FEMME
tagline: Two subjects. One machine. Same refusal to consent.
standard: Written to be verified, not agreed with.
locationNote: This publication does not publish a location. There is no office and no fixed base — the editor travels — so nothing here asserts a country, and neither does the structured data. The only places a country still appears are the legal pages, where POPIA and the choice of governing law are positions to change with advice rather than strings to swap, and the datasets, where South Africa is subject matter rather than an address.
description: FERAL FEMME investigates every industry built on a body that could not agree to it — holding animals and women at equal weight. Public-record reporting, reframed with attribution, across ten industries, with free sustainability tools.

The worksheets and template messages are starting points to adapt, not legal documents. The same notice is printed in full on the first page after the contents of every file, and in the footer of every page.

positioning.lede: We investigate every industry built on a body that could not agree to it — and we hold animals and women at equal weight. Neither is a metaphor for the other. Both are literal.
positioning.body: The cruelty is rarely called cruelty. It is called tradition, testing, farming, research, wellness, self-care. We translate the vocabulary, cite the source, and file the receipt — across fashion, food, beauty, wildlife, medicine, tech, and the advertising that obscures all of it.

method.title: Public-Record Reporting
method.body: Field notes summarise investigations that already exist in the public record — the Sunday Times, the Guardian, Reuters, AP, the New York Times, the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, peer-reviewed studies, parliamentary inquiries, regulatory filings.

method.title: Editorial Synthesis
method.body: Each source is read, reframed in Feral Femme's restrained editorial voice, and connected to the broader pattern of the industry it documents. The original publisher always gets the credit.

method.title: The Visual Essays
method.body: Each frame in the archive carries one documented case — the caption, the source, and the note behind it. Conceptual editorial work rather than documentary photography, and never presented as photographic evidence of a specific event. How the images are made is set out in full under disclosures.

method.title: Sustainability Tools
method.body: Six free interactive tools turn awareness into practice — the Ingredient, Greenwashing, Certification, and Material decoders, the Record Checker, and Where to Act.

method.title: The Research Briefing
method.body: Every field note is sent to subscribers in full on the day it is published, through a provider that reads the site’s own feed. No separate edition, and nothing in the email that is not on the site.

method.title: Self-Funded Platform
method.body: Feral Femme is funded by its readers — donations, and the documents it sells. No advertisers, no industry sponsorship, no editorial conflicts of interest.

newsletter.note: `action` is MailerLite embedded form 197500769051608208 on account 2610955, posted to assets.mailerlite.com rather than the dashboard.mailerlite.com address MailerLite's own share page carries: that one 301s here, and fetch downgrades a POST to a GET when it follows a 301, which would drop the address. `emailField` and `fields` are the names that endpoint expects. The form has double opt-in on, which is why `confirmText` tells the reader to confirm. `group` is the list the form feeds and the briefing sends to; `automationStart` is the cutover before which no note is ever mailed. Clearing `action` degrades the form to a mailto: link.
